title: O debate sobre vacinas em redes sociais: uma análise exploratória dos links com maior engajamento / The debate on vaccines in social networks: an exploratory analysis of links with the heaviest traffic
screen_reason: Content analysis of the 100 most-engaged Portuguese-language links matching the keyword 'vacina' (BuzzSumo; Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest, Reddit; 22 May 2018 - 21 May 2019), 89 of which were still reachable. Every text was coded for veracity using fact-checking procedures, giving a stated item-level share classified as fake news (12/89 = 13.5%). This is a share of items judged for truth/falsity against an external check, so it is CONTENT.

estimates.country: Brasil (textos em lingua portuguesa, contexto brasileiro) / Brazil (Portuguese-language texts, Brazilian context)
estimates.platform: Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest e Reddit (agregados via BuzzSumo) / Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest and Reddit (aggregated via BuzzSumo)
estimates.date: 22 de maio de 2018 a 21 de maio de 2019; busca realizada em 21 de maio de 2019 / 22 May 2018 to 21 May 2019; search run 21 May 2019
estimates.measure_type: % of the most-engaged Portuguese-language 'vacina' links classified as fake news on the researchers' veracity coding
estimates.value_raw: 12/89 (13,5%) fake news; 72/89 (80,9%) informacoes verdadeiras; 3 metafora (3,4%); 2 entretenimento (2,2%)
estimates.denominator: 89 valid links (of the 100 links with the most engagement - shares, likes and comments on Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest and Reddit - retrieved by BuzzSumo for the keyword 'vacina' between 22 May 2018 and 21 May 2019; 11 of the 100 were offline at the time of the study)
estimates.definition: A text coded in the 'veracidade' (veracity) category as fake news: 'utilizando procedimentos de fact checking para determinar se o texto traz informações comprovadas ou se trata de informação falsa' / 'using fact-checking procedures to determine whether the text carries verified information or is false information'. Sensationalist headlines inducing a false meaning were also counted (e.g. a Cuban cancer-vaccine story whose body text was accurate but whose headline claimed a cure).
estimates.misinfo_def: "Uma notícia falsa, ou fake news, pode ser entendida como um boato ou informação intencionalmente enganosa, com o propósito deliberado de gerar desinformação e prejudicar pessoas, grupos sociais, organizações ou mesmo países" / "A false news item, or fake news, can be understood as a rumour or intentionally misleading information, with the deliberate purpose of generating disinformation and harming people, social groups, organisations or even countries"
estimates.source_quote: Em relação à veracidade, 72 textos foram classificados como informações verdadeiras (80,9%) e 12 como fake news (13,5%). Em cinco dos links essa divisão não se aplica: os três casos de metáfora (3,4%) e dois conteúdos enquadrados como entretenimento (2,2%)
estimates.page_loc: Resultados, p. 5 and Figura 4; the same figure appears in the Resumo/Abstract ('as fake news representaram 13,5% dos links com maior engajamento')
estimates.ground_truth_detail: The three authors coded each of the 89 texts on four categories (tema, posicionamento, veracidade, tipo de veículo) following Gill's discourse-analysis steps. Veracity was decided by the authors themselves applying 'procedimentos de fact checking'; for at least one item they contacted the health authority directly to verify a claim ('Em contato com o órgão, confirmamos que a informação é falsa' / 'In contact with the agency, we confirmed the information is false'). No inter-coder reliability statistic and no single external fact-check database; the authors state the thematic division was made 'de modo arbitrário' (arbitrarily).
estimates.moderator_quote: (iii) veracidade, utilizando procedimentos de fact checking para determinar se o texto traz informações comprovadas ou se trata de informação falsa / (iii) veracity, using fact-checking procedures to determine whether the text carries verified information or is false information
estimates.notes: Judgement calls for an adjudicator. (1) CONTENT vs SHARING: the corpus is engagement-RANKED (top 100 by shares + likes + comments), but the denominator counts distinct links, not shares, and no engagement weighting is applied to the 13.5%, so the estimate is a share of items = CONTENT, with denom_selection=curated recording the rank truncation. It is NOT '% of shared links that are false'. (2) The denominator is 89, not 100: 11 links were dead. If a reader wanted the share among items where veracity was applicable, that would be 12/84 = 14.3%, but the paper never states it, so it is not extracted. (3) breadth coded 'false' from the operational coding (true vs false via fact-checking) even though the conceptual definition stresses deliberate intent; one included item is a true-bodied article with a sensationalist, misleading headline, which pushes slightly toward 'misleading'. (4) Country: BuzzSumo was not explicitly geo-restricted, but the keyword is Portuguese, the framing is 'o contexto brasileiro recente' and the outlets are overwhelmingly Brazilian, so country_norm = Brazil. (5) year set to 2019 (the collection date, 21 May 2019); the engagement window straddles May 2018 - May 2019. (6) The search excluded closed groups, where the authors note anti-vaccine content is strongest, so this likely understates vaccine misinformation on Brazilian social media.

missed_or_uncertain: Considered and NOT extracted. (a) '9 of the 18 non-professional outlets propagated vaccine fake news' ('os sites nao profissionais ... totalizaram 18 veiculos'; 'Entre essas paginas, nove propagaram fake news sobre vacinas'). Both counts are verbatim, so 9/18 = 50.0% would be admissible under R8 as a source-level CONTENT share, but the denominator is a doubly sub-selected group (non-professional outlets among the 63 outlets behind the top-89 links), the paper never states the percentage, and no matching figure exists for the 45 professional outlets - a 50% value from that denominator would badly distort any pooled prevalence. Flagged here for an adjudicator to decide. (b) Stance: '78 textos foram classificados como pro-vacina (87,6%) e 8 como contra (9%)' / '78 texts pro-vaccine (87.6%), 8 against (9%)' - an anti-vaccine stance is not a veracity judgement, so this is not a misinformation share. (c) Topic distribution of the 12 fake news items (7 flu 58.3%, 2 meningitis 16.7%, 2 cancer 16.7%, 1 yellow fever 8.3%) and the overlap counts ('Sete deles sao fake news' among the 8 anti-vaccine texts; 'cinco tem posicionamento favoravel' among the 12 fake news) are within-misinformation composition, not prevalence, so no rows. (d) 'sete materias (7,86%) desmentindo informacoes falsas' / 'seven articles (7.86%) debunking false information' - fact-checking content, the opposite of misinformation. (e) Theme shares (ciencia e saude 42.7%, politico 28.1%) are topics, not veracity. (f) Wellcome Global Monitor figures (vaccines effective 84%, safe 79%, South America 82%/81%) are cited from another source - barred by R8 - and are attitudes, not misinformation exposure.

rob.design: Exploratory cross-sectional content/discourse analysis. Frame: BuzzSumo (free trial version) query on the keyword 'vacina', returning the 100 links with the most engagement (shares + likes + comments) on Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest and Reddit between 22 May 2018 and 21 May 2019; search executed 21 May 2019 and exported to a spreadsheet. 11 links were offline, leaving a valid sample of 89 links pointing to 63 web outlets (45 classified 'professional' on four transparency criteria - clear editorial policy, physical address, named authors, cited sources - and 18 'non-professional'). Coding into four categories (theme, stance pro/anti, veracity by fact-checking, outlet type) by the author team following Gill's discourse-analysis steps; no double coding, no kappa, no response rate (not a survey). Acknowledged limitations: closed Facebook/WhatsApp groups, where anti-vaccine content concentrates, are not covered; the thematic split was made 'de modo arbitrario'; engagement-ranked top-100 is not a random sample of vaccine content.
